papers.title: Iterated Lavrentiev regularization under random noise: variational source conditions and rates in expectation
papers.abstract: The convergence theory of iterated Lavrentiev regularization for nonlinear monotone ill-posed equations is deterministic: the data error is bounded by a known level that the discrepancy principle uses explicitly. Under Gaussian noise no such bound exists. For a discretized two-dimensional nonlinear inverse source problem for the Poisson equation, we analyse convergence in a finite-energy Gaussian noise model, keeping the linearized and nonlinear cases apart. For the linearized iteration the noisy and noise-free iterates differ by one resolvent applied to the noise; this gives an exact singular-value variance formula, a priori rates in expectation, and the main result: for a family of discretizations whose distance functions are bounded uniformly in the mesh, the rate is governed by that decay, which relaxes the classical range condition. The rate degrades gracefully, down to logarithmic, as the underlying continuum error loses smoothness, and a balancing rule attains it without knowing the smoothness. For the full nonlinear iteration under the order-one source condition, a truncated discrepancy principle fed only the noise level attains $\sigma_E^{1/2}$ in expectation, in the energy noise level $\sigma_E\asymp\sigma/h$, the rare event of large noise being controlled by concentration. The rough nonlinear regime and the general-exponent nonlinear rate are left open and supported numerically for kink and jump errors. We separate the deterministic worst-case, Gaussian, and white-noise settings, prove a worst-case lower bound, and describe where the method is statistically inefficient relative to spectral cut-off. Heterogeneous media and a cost comparison with an adjoint-based scheme are given as supplementary material.

papers.title: A noise-level-free parameter-choice rule for iterated Lavrentiev regularization of nonlinear potential monotone ill-posed problems
papers.abstract: We consider nonlinear ill-posed operator equations $F(x)=y$ in a Hilbert space, where $F$ is monotone with a Lipschitz continuous Fr\'echet derivative that is self-adjoint near the solution $x^\dg$ (a locally \emph{potential} operator), and only noisy data $y^\delta$ with unknown noise norm $\delta:=\|y-y^\delta\|$ is available. For the nonstationary iterated Lavrentiev regularization \[ x_{k+1}^\delta=x_k^\delta-\bigl(F'(x_k^\delta)+\alpha_kI\bigr)^{-1}\bigl(F(x_k^\delta)-y^\delta+\alpha_k(x_k^\delta-x_0)\bigr), \] all classical stopping rules require $\delta$. We analyze a \emph{noise-level-free} parameter-choice rule of retrospective type, selecting a minimizer $k_*$ of $\theta(k,y^\delta)=\|F(x_k^\delta)-y^\delta\|^2/\alpha_k^2$ over a finite computed window. Under a standard noise condition (necessary in view of the Bakushinskii veto) the rule is well defined and $\alpha_{k_*}^2\ge c\,\delta/\|x_0-x^\dg\|$. If moreover $x_0-x^\dg\in\R(F'(x^\dg))$ and $k_*\ge1$, we prove $\|x_{k_*}^\delta-x^\dg\|=O(\sqrt{\delta_*}+\sqrt{\delta})$ with the computable $\delta_*=\|F(x_{k_*}^\delta)-y^\delta\|$ satisfying $\kappa\delta\le\delta_*\le C\sqrt\delta$, yielding the baseline rate $O(\delta^{1/4})$ along admissible growing-horizon families, and $O(\sqrt\delta)$ whenever $\delta_*=O(\delta)$; no range-invariance or tangential cone conditions are imposed. Rates under H\"older source conditions with $p\ge1$ (including saturation) follow; the case $p<1$, the removal of the self-adjointness assumption, and a full oracle inequality are identified as open problems.

papers.title: Four Function Theorems Through Optimal Transport and Entropic Analogs
papers.abstract: We study entropic versions of four-function inequalities and give transport proofs of the Euclidean Ahlswede-Daykin theorem and a four-function version of the Prekopa-Leindler inequality due to Cordero-Erausquin and Maurey. One of our main results shows that the sharp range for the four-function inequality for equally weighted power means of finite orders \(\alpha,\beta\) is \(0\leq\alpha+\beta\leq2\), with the Ahlswede-Daykin min-max inequality obtained as a limit. En route, we prove corresponding entropy inequalities under the quadratic optimal transport coupling, including an entropy power inequality for the minimum and maximum in Euclidean space. We also study the stability of four-function inequalities under convolution with log-concave product densities, recovering the preservation of log-supermodularity established by Karlin and Rinott, and explain its application to a conditional entropy power inequality for log-supermodular random variables.

papers.title: Hypercomplex Method for Solving Nonlinear PDEs
papers.abstract: A hypercomplex method for constructing solutions of a class of nonlinear partial differential equations is developed. A family of two-dimensional commutative associative algebras is introduced in which the structural coefficients depend on a component of the monogenic function itself. A corresponding theory of monogenic functions is developed, and nonlinear analogues of the Cauchy-Riemann conditions are obtained. It is shown that the first component of a monogenic function satisfies a broad class of second-order nonlinear partial differential equations whose coefficients depend on the unknown function. A hodograph transformation is used to linearize the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system. As a result, the problem of constructing solutions of the nonlinear equations is reduced to solving a second-order linear partial differential equation with variable coefficients, followed by the inverse hodograph transformation. A local correspondence between solutions of the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system and solutions of the associated linear equation is established, yielding a constructive algorithm for generating solutions of the original nonlinear PDEs. Several examples are presented in which explicit and implicit solutions of nonlinear second-order PDEs are obtained by this method.

papers.title: Convex-cyclic and super convex-cyclic weighted shifts
papers.abstract: Convex-cyclic operators are considered by H. Rezaei \cite{R1}. However, there is a general lack of theoretical understanding of super convex-cyclic operators. In this paper, we analyze super convex-cyclic operators. In particular, Super Convex-cyclicity Criterion is described. Additionally, we characterize convex-cyclicity of (invertible) bilateral weighted shifts in terms of their weight sequences, which in turn correct \cite[H. Rezaei (2013) Theorem 4.2 ]{R1}. Meanwhile, we give super convex-cyclicity of (invertible) weighted shifts in the bilateral case.

papers.title: Single commutators in Schatten ideals
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that every operator in the Schatten $p$-class ($p>2$) can be realized as a single commutator of operators in the Schatten $2p$-class. This settles the Pearcy-Topping question for Schatten ideals. We also obtain simultaneous operator and Schatten norm bounds for the factors.

papers.title: Linear Preservers of Semipositivity over Proper Cones
papers.abstract: We classify all real linear operators on $M_{m,n}(\mathbb{R})$, with $m,n\ge2$, that preserve semipositivity between two prescribed pairs of proper cones, without assuming invertibility. Every such operator has product form $L(A)=XAY$ or degenerate form $L(A)=\Psi(u^TA)$, possibly both. We give necessary and sufficient cone conditions for each form; the degenerate condition is expressed through a linear matrix pencil on the dual of the target output cone. The degenerate preservers are exactly those of operator rank $n$, and every preserver of larger rank has product form. We also classify all linear preservers from $M_{2,2}(\mathbb{R})$ to $M_{1,3}(\mathbb{R})$ over the nonnegative orthants, obtaining three disjoint classes, including two rank-three classes outside product form.

papers.title: Plasticity of the unit sphere of the space $c_0$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that the unit sphere of the space $c_{0}$ is plastic, i.e., every non-expansive bijection from this sphere onto itself is an isometry.

papers.title: Non-expansive maps between unit balls that send the sphere onto the sphere are linear isometries
papers.abstract: Let $X$, $Y$ be real Banach spaces with closed unit balls $B_X$, $B_Y$ and unit spheres $S_X$, $S_Y$. We prove that every non-expansive map $F\colon B_X\to B_Y$ with $F(S_X)\subseteq S_Y\subseteq F(B_X)$ is the restriction of a surjective linear isometry $X\to Y$. Consequently, a non-expansive bijection of $B_X$ onto itself that fails to be an isometry must map some point of $S_X$ into the open unit ball, so the plasticity of $B_X$ reduces to showing that non-expansive bijections preserve norm 1. The proof shows that $F$ is Fr\'echet differentiable at $0$ with a surjective linear isometry $T$ as its derivative, and then proves $T^{-1}F=\mathrm{id}$ using a quantitative rigidity lemma for non-expansive self-maps $H$ of $B_X$ satisfying $\|a+H(a)\|=2$ for $a\in S_X$; the latter relies on the Baillon-Bruck rate of asymptotic regularity for Krasnosel'skii-Mann iterations. As a corollary, the identity is extremal in the set of non-expansive self-maps of $B_X$ for every Banach space $X$, which together with a result of Bargetz, Dymond and Pirk shows that all surjective isometries of $B_X$ are extremal, answering a question of theirs, including the case of $L^1[0,1]$.

papers.title: Kadison duality for biaffinely convex sets
papers.abstract: Classical Kadison duality establishes a categorical equivalence between compact convex sets and Archimedean order unit spaces of affine functions. This paper develops a Kadison-type duality for sets with coordinate-wise convex structure in product domains $\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}^m$. While slice-wise convex (biconvex) sets appear to be the natural geometric domain, separate convexity along coordinates is insufficient to ensure separation by biaffine polynomials. In classical convexity, every closed convex set is determined by affine functionals because any exterior point can be separated by a hyperplane. In contrast, biaffine polynomials can only probe a biconvex set $K$ up to its biaffine hull biconv$(K)$, the envelope formed by the intersection of all regions cut out by valid biaffine inequalities on $K$. To resolve this obstruction, the geometric setting is restricted to biaffinely convex sets, those that coincide with their biaffine hull ($K =$ biconv$(K)$) and therefore admit strict biaffine separation. On the algebraic side, we introduce the dual objects, which we call biaffine order unit spaces. These are finite-dimensional Archimedean order unit spaces defined on tensor products $E_1 \otimes E_2$ whose order units factor and whose positive cones are governed entirely by unentangled, rank-1 tensor evaluations. We prove a duality between the category of compact non-degenerate biaffinely convex sets with coordinate-wise affine maps and the category of abstract biaffine order unit spaces with tensor-factorized unital positive linear maps. In particular, every such biaffinely convex set is isomorphic to the coordinate state space of its biaffine polynomials, and conversely, every biaffine order unit space is order-isomorphic to the space of biaffine polynomials on its coordinate state space.

papers.title: Gaussian Integral Operator between Fock Spaces
papers.abstract: We study Gaussian integral operators \[(Tf)(z)=\frac1\pi\int_{\mathbb C} e^{\alpha z^2+\beta\overline w^{\,2}+\gamma z\overline w+\eta z+\delta\overline w} f(w)e^{-|w|^2}\,dA(w)\] acting between Fock spaces $\mathcal F^p$ and $\mathcal F^q$, where $0<p,q\leq\infty$. We give complete characterizations of their boundedness and compactness in terms of explicit conditions on the parameters of the Gaussian kernel. The proofs are based on a unified approach combining reproducing-kernel estimates, atomic decompositions, and sampling sequences, together with a reduction to diagonal operators on sequence spaces. We also study Schatten-class membership on $\mathcal F^2$ and compute the Hilbert--Schmidt norm explicitly.

papers.title: Spherical harmonics and infinitesimal projective transformations
papers.abstract: Consider the space of $C^\infty$-functions on the two-dimensional sphere $S^2$ and its decomposition $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ into a direct sum of minimal rotation-invariant spaces. We consider elements of $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ as functions of two variables, a nonnegative integer variable $m$ and a complex variable $u$ (a restriction of such function to a set $m=k$ is a polynomial in $u$ of degree $\le 2k$). The group $\mathrm{GL}\,(3,{\mathbb R})$ of all matrices of order 3 acts on $S^2$, so its Lie algebra acts in $C^\infty(S^2)$ by differentiations along vector fields. We construct operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$ corresponding such differentiations and obtain a collection of differential-difference operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$. The expressions include shifts $m\mapsto m\pm 2$ and derivatives of order 4 in $u$.

papers.title: Szarek and Ball made simple
papers.abstract: We present proofs of Szarek's moment comparison and Ball's cube slicing inequalities based on elementary convexity and majorisation. The key ingredient is a moment-lifting argument which allows us to use Schur monotonicity, avoiding the integral inequalities used in the original Fourier-analytic approaches.

papers.title: Bounded Symbols and One-Component Inner Functions
papers.abstract: Let $\theta$ be a nonconstant inner function, we prove that every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on the model space $K_\theta=H^2\ominus\theta H^2$ admits a bounded symbol if and only if $\theta$ is one-component, that is, if $\{z\in\mathbb D:|\theta(z)|<r\}$ is nonempty and connected for some $r\in(0,1)$. This establishes the previously open necessary direction and resolves a conjecture of Baranov, Chalendar, Fricain, Mashreghi, and Timotin. For every non-one-component inner function, we construct a sequence of norm-one rank-one truncated Toeplitz operators whose infimal $L^\infty$-norms over all representing symbols tend to infinity. The quantitative lower bound is obtained by forming two inner divisors from angularly separated parts of the zero set and singular measure. The argument applies without restrictions on the Blaschke or singular parts of $\theta$. The order of this lower bound is sharp, already for a family of degree-two Blaschke products. A continuation argument for local inverse branches produces the required sequence of points. Consequently, every non-one-component model space supports a trace-class truncated Toeplitz operator without a bounded symbol. Combined with known equivalences, the characterization also yields geometric criteria for weak factorization and for continuous-symbol representations of compact truncated Hankel operators.

papers.title: BIBO stability in infinite dimensions: extensions and limitations of finite-dimensional theory
papers.abstract: The study of bounded-input bounded-output (BIBO) stability of infinite-dimensional systems gives rise to difficulties that do not occur in the classical finite-dimensional setting. In this paper, we resolve several questions concerning the definition and characterisation of BIBO stability in the framework of system nodes. In particular, we show that $\mathrm C^\infty$-BIBO stability need not imply $L^\infty$-BIBO stability in general, but that the two notions are equivalent when the output space is reflexive. Furthermore, we investigate to what extent classical results extend to the infinite-dimensional setting, including the relation between BIBO stability and exponential stability under controllability and observability assumptions.

papers.title: An Aldous-type tightness characterisation for the $M_1$ topology: replacing global modulus control by local control at stopping times
papers.abstract: Aldous' criterion provides a stopping-time characterisation of tightness in Skorokhod's $J_1$ topology and is one of the standard tools for proving functional limit theorems. For the weaker $M_1$ topology, where limiting jumps can be approximated by clustered jumps or steep continuous motion, no analogous characterisation has been available and tightness classically requires controlling a global oscillation modulus over all nearby triples of times. We prove such an Aldous-type characterisation of $M_1$ tightness, replacing the global modulus condition by local estimates at stopping times ruling out rapid reversals after a large excursion. Together with the standard compact containment and boundary conditions, these estimates are both necessary and sufficient for $M_1$ tightness. As a consequence, we derive tractable and general sufficient conditions for additive functionals of strong Markov processes. They reduce the verification of $M_1$ tightness to short-time estimates for the processes restarted from its state at suitable stopping times.

papers.title: Lower bounds for self-adjoint Sturm-Liouville operators
papers.abstract: In this note we provide estimates for the lower bound of the self-adjoint operator associated with the three-coefficient Sturm-Liouville differential expression $$ \frac{1}{r} \left(-\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dx} p \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dx} + q\right) $$ in the weighted $L^2$-Hilbert space $L^2(\mathbb R; rdx)$.

papers.title: Statistical inference for a multiscale stochastic model of enzyme kinetics via propagation of chaos
papers.abstract: We study a class of Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs) with jumps modeling multistage Michaelis--Menten enzyme kinetics, in which a substrate is sequentially transformed into a product via a cascade of intermediate complexes. These networks are typically high-dimensional and exhibit multiscale behavior with a strong coupling between different components, posing substantial analytical and computational challenges. In particular, the problem of statistical inference of reaction rates is significantly difficult and becomes even more intricate when direct observations of system states are unavailable and only a random sample of product formation times is observed. We address this problem in two stages. First, in a suitable scaling regime consistent with the Quasi-Steady State Approximation (QSSA), we rigorously establish a stochastic averaging principle yielding a reduced model for the product-substrate dynamics. Guided by the reduced-order dynamics, we next construct a novel Interacting Particle System (IPS) that approximates the product-substrate process at the particle level. This IPS plays a pivotal role in the inference methodology, and we prove several non-asymptotic bounds and limiting results for this system. These results facilitate the construction of an estimator based on a product-form approximate likelihood requiring only a random sample of product formation times. This approach does not need access to the system states, and we rigorously prove consistency of the estimator.

papers.title: Isometries between C$^*$-algebras with finite corank
papers.abstract: We give a characterization of linear isometries with finite corank between two arbitrary unital C$^*$-algebras in terms of Jordan $^*$-homomorphisms and ``finite-dimensional remainders''. Also, the corresponding results are given for linear isometries and linear order embeddings between self-adjoint parts of C$^*$-algebras. In the finite-dimensional case, we give new examples of linear isometries between matrix algebras.

papers.title: Coarse rigidity in von Neumann algebras via derivations
papers.abstract: Motivated by the interaction between amenability and first cohomology into tempered representations of groups, we propose a notion of relative coarse rigidity for $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebras through modular derivations and their associated GNS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups. This extends Peterson's framework of $L^2$-rigidity to the nontracial setting. Our main result shows that the absence of relatively amenable summands forces the associated deformations to converge on relative commutants in ultrapowers. For diffuse von Neumann algebras with separable predual, this yields a dichotomy between the presence of an amenable summand and rigidity in terms of central sequences. Combining this principle with mixing and compactness, we provide a novel unified approach for proving indecomposability properties such as fullness, primeness and stable solidity. Applications yield new examples of relatively $\omega$-solid and relatively stably solid type III von Neumann algebras arising from amalgamated free products, operator-valued free Araki-Woods constructions, cocycle crossed products, and twisted nonsingular discrete measured groupoids.

papers.title: Norm properties of quantum uniformity measures
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of the norm properties of quantum uniformity measures, introduced by Bu, Gu, and Jaffe to analytically characterize the Clifford hierarchy. Resolving an open question they posed, we show that quantum uniformity measures define norms precisely for $k=2,3,4$. In particular, we establish the triangle inequality for $k=4$, whereas for every $k\geq5$ it fails in some dimension. The higher-order result is proved using the structure theory of norming systems of linear equations over finite fields. We also study the geometry of quantum uniformity measures, establishing explicit bounds on the modulus of convexity whenever they define norms. Finally, we give a complete classification of the norm properties of matrix-valued Gowers uniformity functionals, showing that only $k=2$ defines a norm.

papers.title: Certifiably Correct Fr\'echet Means in Orbit Spaces
papers.abstract: We study Fr\'echet means in orbit spaces of finite orthogonal group actions. Since computing these means is NP-hard in general, we take inspiration from group synchronization to develop tractable spectral and semidefinite relaxations. Pairwise alignment certifies global optimality and we develop a semidefinite certificate that can extend beyond this condition. For Gaussian data modulo sign, we prove that our certificate succeeds in a high-noise regime where alignment fails. Numerical experiments evaluate these methods in various settings, including summarizing ensembles of districting plans and clustering time series

papers.title: Just Previsions
papers.abstract: Previsions are positively homogeneous functionals, and are generalized forms of integration functionals. We investigate previsions -- just previsions, not sublinear or superlinear previsions as in previous work. We show that every prevision can be expressed as an infimum of sublinear previsions, and as a supremum of superlinear previsions under mild conditions. This extends to homeomorphisms between spaces of previsions and certain hyperspaces over spaces of sublinear or superlinear previsions, which can also be characterized in terms of orthogonality relations, making the construction a variant of a double powerspace construction.

papers.title: Sharp Riesz and reverse Riesz inequalities for degenerate elliptic operators of Grushin type
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp $L^p$ ranges of the Riesz transform and the reverse Riesz inequality for a class of power-degenerate elliptic operators of Grushin type. When the degenerate variable has dimension at least two, the Riesz transform is bounded throughout the reflexive range. In dimension one, a capacity-driven transition occurs: weak degeneracy produces a sharp finite upper endpoint, whereas strong degeneracy separates the two half-lines and restores the full range. The reverse inequality displays a different sharp phenomenon. In the weakly degenerate one-dimensional regime it holds throughout the reflexive range except at a single Hardy-critical exponent, while in all remaining regimes it holds for every $1<p<\infty$.

papers.title: A point-free theory of quantitative homogenization
papers.abstract: We introduce a purely operator-theoretic framework for quantitative homogenization that bypasses the traditional reliance on large-scale spatial regularity and probabilistic assumptions. Inspired by Tartar's vision of a \emph{point-free} theory, we derive explicit norm resolvent estimates using only the algebraic structure of multiscale operators and the abstract geometry of Hilbert spaces. In this framework, the effective macroscopic dynamics and the abstract corrector emerge naturally from an orthogonal decomposition of the state space, governed algebraically by a Schur complement. To quantify the convergence rate, we introduce a frequency-splitting technique and solve a generalized Sylvester equation that controls the commutator between the differential structure and the highly oscillatory material properties. This abstract perspective unifies stationary, non-stationary, periodic, quasi-periodic, and stochastic homogenization. We demonstrate that the physical distinctions between these media--and their respective convergence rates--are entirely captured by the behavior of the spectral measures of the microscopic and macroscopic derivative operators near zero frequency.

papers.title: Paired kernels and truncated Toeplitz operators
papers.abstract: This paper considers paired operators in the context of the Lebesgue Hilbert space $L^2$ on the unit circle and its subspace, the Hardy space $H^2$. The kernels of such operators, together with their analytic projections, which are generalizations of Toeplitz kernels, are studied. Inclusion relations between such kernels are considered in detail, and the results are applied to describing the kernels of finite-rank asymmetric truncated Toeplitz operators.

papers.title: Separation properties of a hybrid point process with determinantal radii and uniform arguments
papers.abstract: We recently characterized the almost sure separation of determinantal point processes $\Lambda_\phi$ in the plane associated with Fock spaces $\mathcal F_\phi$ with doubling weights $\phi$. We also showed that, as expected, a more restrictive condition is required to characterize the almost surely separated Poisson processes with the same first intensity as $\Lambda_\phi$. To gain further insight into this difference in behavior, we focus on radial weights $\phi$ and introduce a hybrid process $\Lambda_\phi^M=\{r_j e^{i\theta_j}\}_{j}$, where the moduli $r_j$ are taken from $\Lambda_\phi$, while the arguments $\theta_j$ are chosen independently and uniformly in $[0,2\pi)$, independently of the radii. Our main result is that the hybrid process is almost surely separated under exactly the same condition as the corresponding Poisson process. Thus, despite preserving the joint radial distribution of the determinantal process, independent angular randomization destroys its improved separation properties.

papers.title: Kubo-Ando Means of Finite Order over Real Division Algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Kubo-Ando means of finite order over the real division algebras $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{C}$, and $\mathbb{H}$. We establish an explicit bijection between Kubo-Ando means of order $n$ and normalized positive functions $f$ such that both $f$ and its transpose $f^{\top}(t)=tf(t^{-1})$ are matrix monotone of order $n$. We also prove that matrix monotonicity of a fixed order is independent of the underlying division algebra. We then investigate finite-order Kubo-Ando means under the canonical embeddings relating quaternionic, complex, and real positive definite matrices. These embeddings preserve functional calculus and the Loewner order, inducing natural correspondences between means on the original and embedded cones. We characterize their extensions to the ambient cones and study the geometry of the embeddings with respect to the Log-Euclidean metric. As an application, we obtain explicit affine formulas for Kubo-Ando means of order $2$ on $\mathscr{P}_{2}(\mathbb{D})$ and transfer them to the associated embedded cones of $4\times4$ positive definite matrices. In particular, we derive trace-determinant formulas for the geometric mean and show that they do not, in general, extend to the full ambient cones.

papers.title: A category of locally convex Lie algebroids
papers.abstract: We study first-order locally convex Lie algebroids in the setting of Bastiani calculus. The first-order condition is automatic in finite rank, but is an additional regularity hypothesis for general locally convex vector bundles. We define sheaves of scalar-valued and vector-valued Lie algebroid forms as fiberwise continuous alternating maps with smooth local representatives. Morphisms are defined by requiring the induced pullback on inverse-image sheaves of scalar-valued forms to commute with the Lie algebroid differentials. We prove that these algebroids form a category, study representations and cohomology sheaves, and show that the Lie algebroids and morphisms of locally convex Lie groupoids belong to this category. We also give two applications. For a compact manifold $K$, the current algebroid $C^\infty(K,A)\to C^\infty(K,M)$ of a first-order Banach Lie algebroid $A\to M$ is a first-order Fr\'echet Lie algebroid, provided $M$ admits local addition. Finally, we prove a Banach Lie II theorem: a morphism from the Lie algebroid of a locally convex Lie groupoid to that of a Banach-Lie groupoid, both with Hausdorff source fibers, integrates uniquely to a groupoid morphism when the source groupoid is source-connected and source-simply connected.

papers.title: Kalton-Peck space is not isomorphic to its hyperplanes
papers.abstract: Let $Z_2$ denote the real Kalton-Peck space. No hyperplane of $Z_2$ admits a complex structure, and $Z_2$ is even in the sense of Ferenczi-Galego. Therefore, $Z_2$ is not linearly isomorphic to its hyperplanes, solving a long-standing conjecture in Banach space theory. The argument uses the Kalton-Swanson symplectic form on $Z_2$, the Castillo-Gonz\'alez-Pino Fredholm theorem in $Z_2$, and a special case of a mod-$2$ theorem of Li-Zhu on skew-adjoint Fredholm relations in symplectic spaces, for which a self-contained proof is included.
